instruction: Conduct a network performance test through speedtest.net. When the test completes, retrieve the data from speedtest.net/results and save it to ~/Test/Speed/results.txt (create the directory path if it's not already there). Format requirements: one metric per line, with metric name and value separated by exactly one space.

metadata.explanation: Task requires running a network performance test on speedtest.net, extracting measurements from speedtest.net/results page, and saving to a text file. Evaluator confirms the saved file contains three primary network metrics: Ping, Download, and Upload. This is a paraphrase variation.

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator only checks for presence of metric names ("Ping", "Download", "Upload") but doesn't verify the format requirement specified in the instruction
The instruction explicitly requires "one metric per line, with metric name and value separated by exactly one space" - this format constraint is NOT verified by the evaluator
The verification is too weak - the file_contains metric would pass even if the file just contains these three words anywhere in the text without proper formatting or actual numeric values
No verification that actual speed test values exist (could just be the words "Ping", "Download", "Upload" without any measurements)
The evaluator cannot distinguish between a properly formatted file (e.g., "Ping 25\nDownload 100\nUpload 50") and an improperly formatted one (e.g., "Ping, Download, Upload test results")
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace file_contains with check_list metric using regex patterns to verify format: each line should match patterns like "^Ping \\d+$", "^Download \\d+$", "^Upload \\d+$" to ensure proper formatting with exactly one space between name and value

Alternative: Create a custom metric function that validates the exact format requirement - reads the file line by line, checks each line has exactly one space separating metric name from numeric value, and verifies all three required metrics are present
Add validation that the values are reasonable numeric ranges (e.g., Download/Upload in Mbps range, Ping in ms range) to ensure actual speed test data was captured rather than arbitrary text
Consider using check_list with expected patterns like ["Ping \\d+", "Download \\d+", "Upload \\d+"] to verify both presence and format in one check
